rationale: The two are structurally almost identical, and B makes nicer small choices: strconv.Itoa instead of fmt.Sprintf, and a field named Value rather than a Product field inside the Product type. But B updates min and max in a single switch, so a palindrome that matches min is never checked against max. While min and max are the same product, an extra factor pair for it is added to min only. In a range whose only palindrome product has several factor pairs, max would therefore report incomplete factors. Setting max = min also shares a slice header, which only works by accident of capacity. A updates min and max with independent if/else chains and builds separate slices, so it is correct in all cases. Correctness beyond the tests outweighs B's minor stylistic advantages.
